expectation.text: Serve two independent Wi-Fi hotspots (separate radios, subnets and bands) from a wired desktop for tablet game streaming and guest devices, without hostapd or an extra DNS daemon, and switch between fixed mode combinations with single commands.

payload.observed: A maintained shell suite does this on Arch/Omarchy with plain NetworkManager: six AP-mode connection profiles (ipv4.method shared, ipv4.never-default, WPA2/RSN, PMF optional) over an internal PCIe MediaTek MT7922 (mt7921e) and a USB MT7921U; each raised hotspot starts its own ephemeral dnsmasq that applies drop-ins in /etc/NetworkManager/dnsmasq-shared.d (dhcp-authoritative, WPAD suppression, larger cache, optional local resolver handed to clients via dhcp-option); the wired interface NATs clients; every mode script resets to a clean off baseline, sets the regulatory country explicitly with a verified retry loop, and a status dashboard reads the live state back. Modes as one-word aliases: web-2g, web-5g, web-dual, web-two (stable tablet AP + external 5 GHz), web-max and dual variants (160 MHz via the separate wpa_supplicant D-Bus recipe), web-off, web-info, web-status, web-manual, web-links. Documented with setup and install scripts at https://github.com/Lobachevski1998/omarchy-web-tools. Live-verified with NetworkManager 1.58.1 running dual AP (5 GHz internal ch36/80 plus 2.4 GHz external ch11/20).
payload.title: Two simultaneous access points with NAT sharing on one desktop using NetworkManager only (web-tools suite)
